entries.evidence: Read the complete new definition and both direct prerequisites SO(p,q) and identity component. The core fully specifies integer domain p,q>=0, p+q>=1, negative-first signature, identity path-component and inherited matrix operations. Proposition 2.6 identifies the identity component as open normal, hence its Lie algebra agrees with SO(p,q). Differentiation gives X^T I+IX=0; X↦IX bijects it with skew matrices, yielding N(N−1)/2. For pq=0 this is compact SO(N); for pq>0 the explicitly displayed cosh/sinh path is in the identity component and unbounded, proving noncompactness. Substituting (p,q)=(r,r+1) or (r,r) gives dimensions r(2r+1), r(2r−1); Etingof §41.2 identifies the split B/D algebras. No assertion identifies SO0 with a universal cover or an adjoint quotient. SO0(1,3) reuses the existing Lorentz owner.
